sources.text:
John Paul II Bright Meadows Square (Polish: Plac Jasne Błonia im. Jana Pawła II), also simply known as the Bright Meadows (Polish: Jasne Błonia), and until 1945 known as Quistorp Meadow (German pronunciation: [ˈkvɪs.tɔrp]; German: Quistorp-Aue), is a garden square in the city of Szczecin, Poland. It is located in the neighbourhood of Downtown-North within the Downtown district, between Moniuszki, Skargi, Szymanowskiego, and Ogińskiego Streets. It borders Jan Kasprowicz Park to the north, and the Szczecin City Hall, a Baroque Revival town hall from 1927, to the south. The garden square was opened in the 1927. It includes the Monument to the Polish Endeavour, a monumental sculpture measuring 22.5 m (73.82 ft) with the three bronze statues of eagles with spread out wings, each placed on a steel column. It was designed by Gustaw Zemła, and unveiled in 1979, to  symbolise and commemorate three generations of Polish inhabitants of the city. The garden square is listed on the voivodeship heritage registry.


== History ==
